title: MATH GAOKAO - 246
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the relationship between two lines given their relationships with a plane.
questions.question: Let \(m\) and \(n\) be two lines in space, and \(\alpha\) be a plane. If \(m \perp \alpha\) and \(n \parallel \alpha\), what is the relationship between \(m\) and \(n\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(m \perp \alpha\), the line \(m\) is perpendicular to every line in the plane \(\alpha\). Because \(n \parallel \alpha\), there exists a line \(n'\) in \(\alpha\) such that \(n \parallel n'\). Since \(m \perp n'\) and \(n \parallel n'\), it follows that \(m \perp n\).
questions.hint: Consider the definition of a line perpendicular to a plane and how parallel lines transfer directional relationships.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the relationship between a line and a plane given perpendicularity conditions of the planes.
questions.question: Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be two planes. If \(\alpha \perp \beta\), and a line \(l\) is perpendicular to \(\alpha\), what is the relationship between \(l\) and \(\beta\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(\alpha \perp \beta\), the normal vector of \(\alpha\) is perpendicular to the normal vector of \(\beta\). The line \(l\) is perpendicular to \(\alpha\), so its direction vector is parallel to the normal vector of \(\alpha\). Therefore, the direction vector of \(l\) is perpendicular to the normal vector of \(\beta\), which means \(l\) is either parallel to \(\beta\) or lies entirely within \(\beta\).
questions.hint: Relate the perpendicularity of planes to their normal vectors, and consider the possible positions of a line whose direction is perpendicular to a plane's normal.

questions.learningObjective: Identify perpendicular lines in a standard geometric solid.
questions.question: In a cube \(ABCD-A_1B_1C_1D_1\), the line \(A_1C_1\) is perpendicular to which of the following lines?
questions.explanation: In the cube, the base \(ABCD\) is a square, so its diagonals are perpendicular, meaning \(AC \perp BD\). Since the top face \(A_1B_1C_1D_1\) is parallel to the base, \(A_1C_1 \parallel AC\). Therefore, \(A_1C_1 \perp BD\). The line \(A_1B\) is not perpendicular to \(A_1C_1\); in fact, \(A_1B\), \(BC_1\), and \(A_1C_1\) are all face diagonals of equal length, forming an equilateral triangle \(A_1BC_1\) where the angle between \(A_1C_1\) and \(A_1B\) is \(60^\circ\). Thus, \(A_1C_1\) is perpendicular only to \(BD\) among the choices.
questions.hint: Project the lines onto the same plane or use the properties of the square base and parallel faces to determine the angles between the lines.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the relationship between the intersection line of two planes and a third plane perpendicular to both.
questions.question: Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be two planes intersecting at line \(l\). If a plane \(\gamma\) is perpendicular to both \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), what is the relationship between \(l\) and \(\gamma\)?
questions.explanation: Let \(n_\alpha\), \(n_\beta\), and \(n_\gamma\) be the normal vectors of planes \(\alpha\), \(\beta\), and \(\gamma\), respectively. Since \(\gamma \perp \alpha\) and \(\gamma \perp \beta\), we have \(n_\gamma \perp n_\alpha\) and \(n_\gamma \perp n_\beta\). This means \(n_\gamma\) is perpendicular to both \(n_\alpha\) and \(n_\beta\), so \(n_\gamma\) is parallel to the cross product \(n_\alpha \times n_\beta\). The direction of the intersection line \(l\) is exactly \(n_\alpha \times n_\beta\). Therefore, \(n_\gamma\) is parallel to \(l\), which implies \(l \perp \gamma\).
questions.hint: Use the normal vectors of the planes. The direction of the intersection line is related to the normal vectors of the two intersecting planes.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the projection of the apex of a regular pyramid onto its base.
questions.question: In a regular triangular pyramid \(S-ABC\) (where the base is an equilateral triangle and the lateral edges are equal), the projection of the vertex \(S\) onto the plane \(ABC\) is the:
questions.explanation: Let \(O\) be the projection of \(S\) onto the plane \(ABC\). Then \(SO \perp ABC\). Since the pyramid is regular, the lateral edges are equal (\(SA = SB = SC\)). By the Pythagorean theorem in the right triangles \(SOA\), \(SOB\), and \(SOC\), we have \(OA = OB = OC\). Thus, \(O\) is equidistant from the vertices \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\). In an equilateral triangle, the point equidistant from all three vertices is the centroid (which coincides with the circumcenter).
questions.hint: Consider the right triangles formed by the altitude of the pyramid and the lateral edges, and use the property of equal lateral edges to find the distances from the projection to the base vertices.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the property of perpendicular planes to determine the relationship between a line and a plane.
questions.question: If two planes \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are perpendicular, and a line \(a\) in \(\alpha\) is perpendicular to the intersection line of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), what is the relationship between \(a\) and \(\beta\)?
questions.explanation: This is a direct application of the property of perpendicular planes. If two planes are perpendicular, then a line in one plane that is perpendicular to their line of intersection is perpendicular to the other plane. Since \(\alpha \perp \beta\) and \(a \subset \alpha\) with \(a\) perpendicular to the intersection line, it follows that \(a \perp \beta\).
questions.hint: Recall the theorem regarding the conditions under which a line in one of two perpendicular planes is perpendicular to the other plane.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the possible positions of a line given its perpendicularity to another line and a plane.
questions.question: Let \(a\) and \(b\) be two lines in space, and \(\alpha\) be a plane. If \(a \perp b\) and \(a \perp \alpha\), what is the relationship between \(b\) and \(\alpha\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(a \perp \alpha\), the direction vector of \(a\) is parallel to the normal vector of \(\alpha\). The condition \(a \perp b\) means the direction vector of \(b\) is perpendicular to the direction vector of \(a\). Therefore, the direction vector of \(b\) is perpendicular to the normal vector of \(\alpha\). This implies that the line \(b\) is either parallel to the plane \(\alpha\) or lies entirely within the plane \(\alpha\).
questions.hint: Relate the perpendicularity of lines to their direction vectors, and consider what it means for a line's direction vector to be perpendicular to a plane's normal vector.

questions.learningObjective: Identify planes that are perpendicular to a given plane in a cube.
questions.question: In a cube \(ABCD-A_1B_1C_1D_1\), the plane \(A_1BD\) is perpendicular to which of the following planes?
questions.explanation: In the cube, the diagonal \(BD\) of the base is perpendicular to the diagonal \(AC\) of the base. Also, \(BD\) is perpendicular to the vertical edge \(AA_1\). Since \(AC\) and \(AA_1\) are two intersecting lines in the plane \(ACC_1A_1\), it follows that \(BD \perp\) plane \(ACC_1A_1\). Because \(BD\) lies in the plane \(A_1BD\), the plane \(A_1BD\) is perpendicular to the plane \(ACC_1A_1\). The plane \(BB_1D_1D\) intersects \(A_1BD\) at \(BD\), but they are not perpendicular.
questions.hint: Look for a line in the plane \(A_1BD\) that is perpendicular to two intersecting lines in one of the given options.

questions.learningObjective: Determine perpendicular relationships in a pyramid with a rhombus base.
questions.question: Let \(PA\) be perpendicular to the plane of the rhombus \(ABCD\). Which of the following statements is true?
questions.explanation: Since \(ABCD\) is a rhombus, its diagonals are perpendicular, so \(AC \perp BD\). Because \(PA \perp\) plane \(ABCD\), \(PA \perp BD\). Since \(AC\) and \(PA\) are two intersecting lines in the plane \(PAC\), we have \(BD \perp\) plane \(PAC\). The line \(PC\) lies in the plane \(PAC\), so \(BD \perp PC\). The statement \(PB \perp CD\) is false because \(AB\parallel CD\), and \(AB\) is the orthogonal projection of \(PB\) onto the base plane. Thus, the correct answer is B.
questions.hint: Use the properties of the rhombus diagonals and the perpendicularity of the lateral edge to the base to find a plane that is perpendicular to one of the diagonals.

questions.concept: Plane perpendicularity in a regular pyramid
questions.learningObjective: Determine the perpendicular planes in a regular quadrangular pyramid.
questions.question: In a regular quadrangular pyramid \(S-ABCD\), the plane \(SAC\) is perpendicular to the plane:
questions.explanation: In a regular quadrangular pyramid, the base \(ABCD\) is a square, and the projection of the apex \(S\) is the center \(O\) of the base. The plane \(SAC\) contains the diagonal \(AC\) and the altitude \(SO\). Since \(ABCD\) is a square, \(BD \perp AC\). Since \(SO \perp\) plane \(ABCD\), \(SO \perp BD\). Thus, \(BD \perp\) plane \(SAC\). Because \(BD\) lies in the plane \(ABCD\), the plane \(ABCD\) is perpendicular to the plane \(SAC\).
questions.hint: Consider the altitude of the pyramid and the diagonals of the square base to find a line in the base that is perpendicular to the plane \(SAC\).
